skill.name: linux-shell-scripting
skill.description: Provides Bash script templates for Linux backups, monitoring, user management, log analysis, networking, and maintenance automation.
skill.summary: Create practical Linux shell scripts for common administration and automation tasks.
skill.author: sickn33

security_audit.summary: Most medium detections are Markdown code fences, inline examples, or normal Bash syntax, and those were dismissed as false positives. Confirmed risks remain where the skill teaches privileged package and service changes, user account and password-file inspection, cron or background persistence, destructive deletion, credential exposure, and remote script execution. No prompt-injection text was found in SKILL.md.

remediation.issue: Privileged package, user, service, and cron examples can change host state.
remediation.suggestion: Add explicit consent steps, least-privilege guidance, allowlists, dry-run modes, and warnings before sudo or cron operations.

remediation.issue: Password-file and account reporting examples expose local account inventory.
remediation.suggestion: Limit these scripts to authorized administration, avoid broad account enumeration, and protect generated reports with restrictive permissions.

remediation.issue: Cleanup examples delete files from user-selected paths.
remediation.suggestion: Add path allowlists, dry-run output, confirmation prompts, root-path guards, and audit logs before running rm.

remediation.issue: Credential examples store or print sensitive values.
remediation.suggestion: Use environment variables, secret stores, protected files, or interactive prompts, and avoid echoing generated passwords by default.

remediation.issue: Remote execution examples can run arbitrary scripts on remote hosts.
remediation.suggestion: Require explicit host and script validation, SSH identity checks, command logging, and authorization notes before remote execution.

semantic_findings.title: Plaintext Credential Handling in Database Backup Template
semantic_findings.description: The database backup template sets a db_pass variable and passes the password on the mysqldump command line. Users may copy this pattern and expose database credentials through process listings or saved scripts.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The template directly includes a password variable and uses it in a command argument. The value is a placeholder, but the pattern encourages unsafe credential handling.

semantic_findings.title: Generated Password Printed to Output
semantic_findings.description: The password generator prints the generated password to standard output. This can expose secrets in terminal scrollback, logs, shared transcripts, or monitoring tools.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The script assigns a generated password and immediately echoes it. The risk depends on where output is captured, but the exposure path is clear.

semantic_findings.title: Destructive File Deletion Template
semantic_findings.description: The cleanup template accepts a directory and age value, then deletes matching files with rm. It lacks a dry-run mode, path allowlist, confirmation, or protection against accidental broad deletion.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The template contains a direct find command that executes rm against a user-selected directory. The missing safeguards make the destructive behavior high confidence.

semantic_findings.title: Remote Script Execution Template
semantic_findings.description: The remote execution template sends a local script to a remote host over SSH and runs it with Bash. This is high impact if the remote host or script path is untrusted or user-controlled.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The template explicitly executes a script on a remote server from configurable parameters. That is a clear remote execution capability, even though it can be legitimate.

semantic_findings.title: Unvalidated Privileged Service Control
semantic_findings.description: The service restart template accepts a service name argument and passes it to sudo systemctl start or restart. Without allowlisting, a user can target sensitive services for privileged changes.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The service name is argument-controlled and used in privileged systemctl commands. The static sudo finding catches privilege use, but this adds the missing input-control context.

content.value_statement: Linux administrators need repeatable scripts for backups, monitoring, and maintenance. This skill provides Bash templates and guidance for common operational tasks.
actual_capabilities: Creates Bash templates for local, remote, and database backups.
Builds CPU, disk, health, and system information monitoring scripts.
Drafts user account, password expiry, and password generation scripts.
Generates log analysis scripts for system and web server logs.
Provides network connectivity, interface, and website uptime checks.
Outlines package, service, cron, cleanup, rsync, and Git automation tasks.
limitations: Templates require review before use on production systems.
Several examples require Linux tools and may not work on every distribution.
Privileged examples need sudo or root permissions and can change system state.
The skill does not add full error handling, rollback, or compliance controls by default.

use_cases.title: Automate Backups
use_cases.description: Create repeatable backup and rotation scripts for application files or databases.

use_cases.title: Monitor Linux Hosts
use_cases.description: Generate scripts that report CPU, disk, uptime, users, and service status.

use_cases.title: Review Operational Logs
use_cases.description: Build scripts that summarize error logs, web requests, and network status for authorized systems.

prompt_templates.title: Create a Backup Script
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a Bash script that backs up one directory to another directory with a timestamped archive. Include simple validation and clear status messages.

prompt_templates.title: Add Monitoring Alerts
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a Bash script that checks CPU and disk usage on a Linux host. Add thresholds, readable output, and a place for notification logic.

prompt_templates.title: Analyze Logs Safely
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a Bash script that summarizes recent error entries from a system log. Include input validation, output file naming, and permission notes.

prompt_templates.title: Design Production Automation
prompt_templates.prompt: Design a production-ready Bash maintenance script for backups, cleanup, and service checks. Include dry-run mode, logging, safeguards, and rollback notes.

output_examples.input: Request for a daily backup workflow with rotation.
output_examples.output: A Bash script plan with configurable source paths, timestamped archives, retention limits, validation checks, and scheduling notes.

output_examples.input: Request for a Linux health report script.
output_examples.output: A structured report workflow that captures uptime, load, memory, disk use, top processes, and a readable output file.
A maintenance script design with dry-run behavior, path restrictions, age filters, logging, and explicit confirmation before deletion.

best_practices: Test every generated script in a non-production environment first.
Use least privilege, explicit paths, quoted variables, and clear logging.
Add dry-run modes and confirmations before destructive or privileged actions.
anti_patterns: Running generated scripts as root without reviewing each command.
Embedding plaintext passwords or tokens directly in shell scripts.
Scheduling cron jobs or deletion tasks without logging and rollback plans.

faq.question: Can this skill run shell commands automatically?
faq.answer: No. It provides templates and guidance. Users must review and run scripts in their own environment.

faq.question: Does it support non-Linux systems?
faq.answer: It targets Linux and Unix-style Bash environments. Some commands may need changes on macOS or BSD systems.

faq.question: Are the templates production ready?
faq.answer: They are starting points for production scripts. Add environment-specific validation, logging, rollback, and access controls.

faq.question: Can it help with backups and retention?
faq.answer: Yes. It includes examples for archive creation, remote backup, database dump workflows, and backup rotation.

faq.question: How should privileged commands be handled?
faq.answer: Review every privileged command, use least privilege, and require explicit approval before changing packages, services, users, or schedules.

faq.question: Is it useful with Claude, Codex, and Claude Code?
faq.answer: Yes. The skill can guide Claude, Codex, and Claude Code when drafting Linux Bash automation tasks.
